title: Confidence homogeneity: do models share the same miscalibration on the same items?

original_idea.body:
# Confidence homogeneity

Elicit verbalized/logit confidence from several models on a labeled QA set; identify high-confidence-wrong items per model and test whether these overlap across models more than chance. Inference + stats.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Level 4: strong chain — correlated overconfidence defeats confidence-based abstention/escalation, a concrete frontline safety control.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Level 5: elicit confidence, find high-confidence-wrong overlap; standard tooling and labeled QA, beginner-accessible.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Level 5: tightly scoped single experiment (confident-wrong overlap vs chance) with clear metric.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Level 4: open/API models + public QA, weak lab incentive, no internal access.

novelty.reasoning: Calibration studied; the correlated-miscalibration-across-models angle is plausibly open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Combines calibration with homogeneity; correlated-miscalibration angle plausibly open.
